text: My main symptom is Painful ulcerative lesion on the right leg. I also have Lesion has a central necrotic base and purplish irregular borders, History of ant bite at the site of the lesion, Pitting pedal edema of the lower extremities, Dilated tortuous veins in both lower legs. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Cellulitis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pyoderma Gangrenosum (PG) secondary to Crohn's disease.

The lesion's rapid progression from an ant bite to a painful ulcer with central necrosis and purplish borders is characteristic of PG, which often presents with an "autoamputation" phenomenon where trauma triggers the ulceration. Your history of Crohn's disease and diabetes are significant risk factors for this condition. The previous diagnosis of cellulitis is unlikely given the specific morphology and your autoimmune background; PG requires a clinical diagnosis and response to immunosuppression rather than antibiotics.
